title: Quasi-coherent cohomology of a quasi-compact quasi-separated space vanishes above dimension
statement: Let $B$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $X$ be an algebraic space over $B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume $X$ is quasi-compact (it admits a quasi-compact surjective etale scheme atlas) and quasi-separated (its absolute representable diagonal $X\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X$ is quasi-compact, meaning that every scheme base change has quasi-compact inverse images of quasi-compact opens). Give $|X|$ the quotient topology from an etale atlas [def-a1-space-point-topology], and let $\dim|X|$ be its topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with $\dim\varnothing=-\infty$. Let $d\geq0$ be an integer with $\dim|X|\leq d$. For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $G$ on the small etale ringed site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], one has $H^q(X,G)=0$ for every integer $q>d$. Here $H^q$ is the right derived functor of module global sections, computed by an injective resolution in all module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. No Noetherian, coherence, separatedness, properness or flatness hypothesis is imposed beyond quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness.

source.place: Tag 0A4R (lemma-vanishing-above-dimension), part (1), with the preceding paragraph identifying chart dimension and topological Krull dimension for quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] with $S=B$ and $S\prime=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. It retains the scheme charts, fibre products, small etale ringed site and structure sheaf; the same chart quotient gives the same point space. Thus quasi-compactness, the absolute quasi-separatedness hypothesis, dimension and the cohomology in the statement are unchanged. Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ from now on. By [lem-sfb-qcqs-space-splitting-filtration] choose $n\geq1$, quasi-compact opens $\varnothing=U_{n+1}\subset U_n\subset\cdots\subset U_1=X$, and surjective etale $f_p:V_p\to U_p$ with $V_p$ quasi-compact separated schemes, isomorphisms over the reduced complements $T_p=U_p\setminus U_{p+1}$, and $U_n\simeq V_n$. Put $W_p=U_{p+1}\times_{U_p}V_p$. The pair $(U_{p+1}\subset U_p,V_p\to U_p)$ is an elementary distinguished square by precisely the stated complement isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0A4R(1), finite filtration paragraph; Tag 07ST (decent-spaces.tex); change of base required by the absolute-base formulation of 07ST

proof.text: Every $U_p$ is quasi-separated: its absolute diagonal is the base change of the absolute diagonal of $X$ along $U_p\times U_p\to X\times X$, and quasi-compactness is preserved by base change [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] its point space is the corresponding open subspace of $|X|$; hence [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone] gives $\dim|U_p|\leq d$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-etale-atlas-topological-dimension] to $U_p\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and its atlas $V_p$: $\dim|V_p|=\dim|U_p|\leq d$. The open immersion $U_{p+1}\to U_p$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence]. Its base change $W_p\to V_p$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]; testing the latter over the quasi-compact scheme $V_p$ shows that $W_p$ is quasi-compact. It is an open subscheme of $V_p$ by the open-subspace chart clause of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Its dimension is at most $d$ by open-subspace dimension monotonicity. Since $V_p$ is separated, it is quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]; restriction of its diagonal gives the same for $W_p$. Thus both $V_p$ and $W_p$ are qcqs schemes, and their underlying spaces are spectral by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral].

source.place: Tag 0A4R(1), initial dimension remarks and scheme-chart hypotheses; Tags 0A4H/0A4J; 073B and 094L for the finiteness and spectral checks

proof.text: For $A=U_p,V_p,W_p$ write $G_A$ for etale restriction of $G$. The localized ringed-site identifications of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model] identify this with tensor pullback, because the structure sheaf is restricted without a change of rings. Each $G_A$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent]. For a scheme among these objects, [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] gives a quasi-coherent Zariski module $F_A$ whose associated etale module is $G_A$. Its module cohomology on the etale site is canonically $H^q(A,F_A)$ on the Zariski site by [lem-sfb-qcoh-cohomology-etale-pullback-naturality]. By [lem-sc-zariski-module-abelian-cohomology-agree] the latter is the cohomology of the underlying abelian sheaf. Consequently [lem-sfb-spectral-space-cohomology-dimension] applied to the spectral spaces from step 2 gives $H^q(V_p,G_{V_p})=H^q(W_p,G_{W_p})=0$ for $q>d$. The same holds for $U_n\simeq V_n$. Moreover, apply [lem-sfb-spectral-module-top-degree-restriction] to $(|V_p|,\mathcal O_{V_p})$, $F_{V_p}$ and its quasi-compact open $W_p$. It makes $H^d(V_p,F_{V_p})\to H^d(W_p,F_{V_p}|_{W_p})$ surjective. The restriction inverse in the quasi-coherent equivalence identifies $F_{V_p}|_{W_p}$ with $F_{W_p}$, and the displayed pullback-naturality square of the cohomology comparison transports this particular restriction map to $H^d(V_p,G_{V_p})\to H^d(W_p,G_{W_p})$. Thus this last map is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0A4R(1), scheme comparison and spectral cohomology input; Tags 03DW, 0A3G(1),(2) and 01F1

proof.text: For any one of the small etale ringed sites used here, a module map $\mathcal O\to I$ is determined by its values on $1$: these are compatible sections of $I$, and conversely such a family defines the map by $a\mapsto a s$. Thus the complex $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(\mathcal O[0],I^{\bullet})$ is exactly $\Gamma(I^{\bullet})$, using [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. The K-injective Hom computation of [lem-sfb-derived-internal-hom-sections-model], with first complex $\mathcal O[0]$, therefore identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_A)}(\mathcal O_A,G_A[q])$ with $H^q(A,G_A)$; an ordinary injective resolution is K-injective by [lem-sp-kinjective-computes]. This computation also identifies the restriction maps, since the formula on each complex is restriction of its compatible sections. Specialize [lem-sfb-space-derived-hom-mayer-vietoris] to the distinguished square in step 1 and $E=\mathcal O_{U_p}[0]$, $F=G_{U_p}[0]$. Its exact etale restrictions of $E$ are the structure sheaves. The resulting long exact sequence contains $$H^{q-1}(U_{p+1},G)\oplus H^{q-1}(V_p,G)\longrightarrow H^{q-1}(W_p,G)\longrightarrow H^q(U_p,G)\longrightarrow H^q(U_{p+1},G)\oplus H^q(V_p,G),$$ with the first arrow the difference of the two restrictions. Here the notation suppresses the indicated etale restrictions of $G$.

source.place: Tag 08H9 (lemma-mayer-vietoris-hom), specializing E to the structure sheaf; Mayer-Vietoris reformulation of the localization step in Tag 0A4R(1)

proof.text: Descend on $p$ from $n$ to $1$, proving the simultaneous assertion $H^q(U_p,G_{U_p})=0$ for all integers $q>d$. The base $p=n$ is step 3. For $p<n$ assume the assertion for $p+1$, and fix $q>d$. The final term of the exact segment in step 4 is zero by the induction hypothesis and step 3. If $q>d+1$, then $H^{q-1}(W_p,G)=0$ by step 3, so exactness gives $H^q(U_p,G)=0$. If $q=d+1$, the restriction from the $V_p$ summand of the first term onto $H^d(W_p,G)$ is surjective by step 3; its negative is still surjective. Hence the boundary into $H^{d+1}(U_p,G)$ is zero, and exactness plus the vanishing of the final term again gives $H^{d+1}(U_p,G)=0$. These two cases exhaust integer $q>d$. At $p=1$ this is the required vanishing on $X$. The argument also covers $d=0$ and empty strata: all restrictions to the empty space have zero target, and the same exact segment applies.
